name: Beetle
description: Dung beetles navigate by Milky Way polarization gradient — the only known non-human galactic navigator. Bombardier beetles synthesize binary chemical explosions at 100C. Bioluminescent firefly flash patterns encode species-specific optical signals.

core_attributes.neurology: dorsal rim area polarization detectors, chemical synthesis glands, bioluminescence organs
core_attributes.pattern: galactic polarization navigation, binary chemical synthesis, bioluminescent encoding

scope.definition: Orientation accuracy of dung beetle (Scarabaeus satyrus) rolling in straight line using Milky Way galactic polarization gradient — deviation from straight path under full Milky Way vs overcast conditions.

evidence.source: Dacke et al. (2013) 'Dung beetles use the Milky Way for orientation', Current Biology 23:298-300.
cross_domain_examples: dung beetles under Milky Way maintain 0.91 straight-line fidelity vs 0.42 under overcast sky
insects inside planetarium: orientation disrupted when Milky Way band removed from projection
monarch butterfly time-compensated sun compass: analogous celestial navigation by single insect lineage

scope.falsifiability: If dung beetles show no change in straight-line fidelity between Milky Way and overcast conditions in controlled planetarium experiments, galactic navigation is not the mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Navigation advantage applies specifically to nocturnal ball-rolling phase when sun/moon absent. Only Milky Way-class brightness gradient sufficient — individual star navigation not demonstrated.

scope.definition: Species-specificity of bombardier beetle binary chemical spray — proportion of conspecific predators deterred per defensive spray event vs non-predator controls, in field assay studies.

evidence.source: Eisner & Aneshansley (1982) 'Spray aiming in bombardier beetles', Science 215:83-85; Dean et al. (1990) 'Defensive spray of the pygmy grasshopper', Journal of Insect Physiology.
cross_domain_examples: bombardier beetle deters 0.88 of toad attacks via 100°C quinone spray pulsed at 500 Hz
spray aim accuracy: 270° directional coverage achieved by abdominal rotation — engineered equivalent is radar jamming
monarch butterfly chemical defense (cardenolides): analogous aposematic chemical deterrence from sequestered toxins

scope.falsifiability: If bombardier spray contact shows no statistically higher deterrence rate than control chemical at same temperature, spray temperature is not the deterrence mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Deterrence effectiveness is predator-experience-dependent — naive predators are more deterred than experienced ones. Spray volume is limited; sustained predator attacks can overcome chemical defense.

scope.definition: Species-specificity of firefly flash pattern recognition — proportion of correct species identification by female fireflies responding to male flash sequences vs random flash patterns at equivalent intensity.

evidence.source: Lloyd (1966) 'Studies on the flash communication system in Photinus fireflies', Miscellaneous Publications of the University of Michigan Museum of Zoology 130:1-95; Lewis & Cronin (2018) bioluminescence review.
cross_domain_examples: Photinus pyralis females respond to species-specific 0.3 s flash at 6 s interval with 0.87 specificity
Photuris females mimic Photinus flash to lure males — response specificity enables predatory mimicry
deep-sea Aequorea bioluminescence: analogous species-specific light organ pattern for mate recognition

scope.falsifiability: If female fireflies respond equally to conspecific and heterospecific flash patterns at equivalent intensity, temporal encoding is not the species-recognition mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Flash pattern specificity depends on temperature — flash duration changes 20% over 10°C range, requiring receiver compensation. Measurement requires controlled temperature and dark environment.
